title: Introductory Psychology
description: Facts, principles, and concepts which are basic to understanding human behavior.

title: Health, Happiness, and Academic/Professional Success
description: Evidenced-based skills to help in multiple areas of life on and off campus to include academics, mental and physical health, social connections and relationships.

title: Academic and Career Opportunities in Psychology
description: Information about careers in psychology. Includes identification of career-related strengths and interests and information on post-baccalaureate options in psychology and related fields. Introduction to resources in Psychology Undergraduate Advising and Career Services.

title: Introduction to Cognitive Psychology
description: Basic principles and research in animal and human cognition.

title: Developmental Psychology
description: Psychological development of normal individual from conception through childhood, adolescence, and maturity. Emphasis on interdependence of various periods of the individual’s life. Not open to students with credit in

title: Introduction to Physiological Psychology
description: Elementary physiology of the nervous system. Physiological mechanisms underlying the psychological phenomena of sensation, perception, emotion, arousal, motivation, learning and memory, and cortical specialization.

title: Statistical Methods in Psychology
description: Quantitative methods in psychology for producing, analyzing, and interpreting data. Sampling, basic research designs, describing distributions, correlation, regression, applications of normal probability curve, confidence intervals, and tests of significance. Analysis and interpretation of data using statistical, spreadsheet, and word processing software.

title: Statistical Methods in Psychology Support
description: Required support course for

title: Data Analysis in Psychology
description: Statistical and graphic analysis and interpretation of psychological data using computer technology. Activities involve statistical, spreadsheet, and word processing software. Not open to students with credit in

title: Experimental Topics
description: Selected topics.

title: Introduction to Research Methods in Psychology
description: Methods used to answer questions in psychology, including case study, observation, survey, experimental, and field study procedures. Class projects using these methods, interpreting results and report writing; critically evaluating research findings.

title: Behavior Modification
description: Contingencies of reinforcement, stimulus control, response shaping, aversive control, and other basic principles of operant behavior applied to understanding and modification of human behavior.

title: Industrial and Organizational Psychology
description: Broad-based survey of content areas in industrial (selection, job analysis, job performance, individual differences assessment, training) and organizational (work attitudes, stress and well-being, motivation, teams, leadership, diversity/fairness) psychology. Underlying psychological principles that influence human behavior in the workplace.
notes: Not open to students with credit in PSY 420 or PSY 421

title: Psychology of Infant and Child Development
description: Psychological development of normal child from infancy through childhood focusing on physical, social, cognitive, and linguistic aspects of development.

title: Psychology of Adolescent and Early Adult Development
description: Psychological development of individual from adolescence through early adulthood focusing on physical, social, and cognitive aspects of development.

title: Developmental Psychopathology
description: Cognitive, affective, and social aspects of abnormal development from childhood through adolescence. Consideration, within a developmental framework, of etiological theories and factors, problem expression and treatment issues.

title: Social Psychology
description: Major problems and findings concerning group behavior and group membership, the socialization of the individual, and processes of social interaction.

title: Psychology and Culture
description: Impact of culture in each of psychology’s major areas, theories, and empirical findings.

title: Chicana and Chicano Psychology
description: Evolution of psychology of Chicanos with emphasis on understanding underlying roots and foundations. Empirical research conducted with Chicanos in areas of psychology, psychiatry, and mental health.

title: Psychopathology
description: Causes and treatment of abnormal behavior with emphasis on major behavior disorders.

title: Psychology of Personality
description: Major theoretical approaches to individual differences and the study of the person. Techniques of personality assessment. Selected research findings.

title: Stress, Trauma, and the Psychological Experience of Combat
description: Physiology, psychological experience, historical context, and measurement of stress, to include family and workplace stress, large scale traumatic events and disasters, combat and war. Coping with stress, loss, emotional wounds, and bereavement. Treatment, diagnosis, and potential for personal growth.

title: Psychology of Human Sexual Behavior
description: Evaluation of behavioral and physiological data of normal, aberrant, and dysfunctional human sexual behavior, including description of available treatment methods.

title: Forensic Psychology
description: How psychological research and theory informs legal processes. Behavioral analysis, criminal investigation, eyewitness identification, jury selection, juvenile forensics and death penalty cases, mental competencies, police work, school bullying, sexual abuse issues, and threat assessment.

title: Behavioral Neuroscience
description: Biological and physiological underpinnings of behavior: genetics, hormones, transmitters, plasticity/regeneration, development, and metabolism/nutrition. Analysis of their role in normal behavior, psychopathology, neurological disorders, and treatment of behavioral disturbances.

title: Neuropsychology
description: Characterization of human brain-behavior relationships derived from neuropsychometric studies of healthy, neuropsychiatric and brain damaged populations. Emphasis on functional neuroanatomy and the effects of abnormal brain development and disease on processes such as cognition, memory, language, visual-spatial, and other functions.

title: Cognitive Neuroscience
description: Functional organization of the human brain, including sensorimotor and cognitive systems and their functional interactions; development and evolution; normal and pathological plasticity. Approaches applied to healthy human brain, such as neuroimaging and event-related potentials.

title: Drugs and Behavior
description: Fundamentals of regulation, administration, tolerance, dependence, and physiological activity of drugs. Effects of stimulants, depressants, opiates, psychedelics, and psychotherapeutic drugs on the nervous system and on cognitive, personality, and behavioral functioning.

title: Psychological Testing and Measurement
description: Measurement theory and the basic principles of testing. Selection, construction and critical evaluation of group tests of intelligence, personality, aptitude, interest and achievement.

title: Intermediate Cognitive Psychology
description: Research and theory on attention, language, learning, memory, thinking, and understanding.

title: Sensation and Perception
description: Theory and research in sensory and perceptual processes.

title: Health Psychology
description: Behavioral components of major illnesses and causes of death and disability. Primary prevention of health problems through behavior change and psychological features of the health care system.

title: Advanced Research Methods Laboratory
description: Use of research design, quantitative methods, and research reports as applied to all areas of psychology.

title: Advanced Topics in Industrial Psychology
description: Advanced study in industrial psychology. Psychological principles and research methodology applied to personnel management problems. Selected topics may include personnel selection, job analysis, job performance, individual differences assessment, training, and diversity/fairness issues related to implementing personnel systems.
notes: See Class Schedule for specific content

title: Advanced Topics in Organizational Psychology
description: Advanced study in organizational psychology. Psychological principles and research methodology applied to human behavior at work. Selected topics may include work attitudes, stress and worker well-being, motivation, teams, leadership, organizational development, and diversity/fairness issues related to implementing organizational systems.
notes: See Class Schedule for specific content

title: Prejudice and Stereotypes
description: Classic and contemporary theories and research on prejudice and stereotyping to include origin and forms of phenomena, consequences, and approaches aimed at reducing them.

title: Introduction to Counseling and Therapy
description: Theory, methods, and research in psychological approaches to personality and behavior change.

title: Psychology of Death and Bereavement
description: Latest psychological research and clinical practice in the area of death and dying, geared to assisting the student in appropriate ways of aiding both the dying and the bereaved in coming to terms with death.

title: Intermediate Statistics for Psychological Research
description: Theoretical foundations of statistics including probability theory, distribution theory, and statistical inference. Model-based statistical comparisons. Application of statistical theory to psychological research questions.

title: Academic or Psychological Counseling Experiences
description: Individual supervision of academic or psychological counseling experiences, geared to acquisition of counseling and communication skills.
notes: No more than nine units of Psychology 491,

title: Responsible Conduct in Scientific Research
description: Responsible conduct in scientific research. Topics include conflict of interest, plagiarism, reporting of scientific results, authorship, responsible use and care of animals, responsible use of human subjects.

title: Special Study: Techniques for Teaching and Tutoring in Psychology
description: Practical knowledge and experience in psychology instruction and advanced content in a specific area of psychology.
notes: No more than nine units of

title: Field Placement in Psychology
description: Students will be assigned to various community agencies and work under joint supervision of an agency supervisor and course instructor, attend class meetings, and staff conferences.
notes: No more than nine units of PSY 491, PSY 494, PSY 495 may be counted toward the major and no more than 12 units of courses numbered PSY 491, PSY 494, PSY 495, PSY 497, PSY 499 may be counted toward the major.

title: Selected Topics in Psychology
description: Intensive study in specific areas of psychology.

title: Senior Project
description: Individual investigation and APA-style report on a research project.
notes: No more than nine units of Psychology 497 and

title: Undergraduate Honors Thesis
description: Directed research in psychology and completion of honors thesis. Required of students graduating with a Certificate of Recognition of Psychology Honors Thesis.

title: Special Study
description: Individual study, including library or laboratory research and a written report.
notes: No more than nine units of

title: Advanced Neuropsychology
description: Biological bases of neuropsychological function and dysfunction, relationships between brain structure and function, neuropsychological assessment tools.

title: Systems Neuroscience
description: Neuroanatomy and neurophysiology of the mammalian through a signals and systems lens to include auditory, cell physiology, motor and limbic systems, neural development, simple neural models, somatosensory, and visual components. Neuroimaging physics.

title: Foundations of Neuroimaging
description: Physical and mathematical foundations of diffusion, functional, structural, perfusion MRI, and fMRI time series analysis. Cortical-surface based reconstruction and data analysis. Neural basis, localization, and recording of EEG and MEG signals.

title: Selected Topics in Psychology
description: Intensive study in specific areas of psychology.

title: Research Orientation
description: Research in psychology. All master’s degree students are required to enroll in this course.

title: Advanced Research Methods in Psychology
description: Diverse research methods across different areas of psychology. Interdependence of theory and methodology in research to include design, measurement, and validity.

title: Seminar in Industrial Psychology
description: Survey course applying psychological principles and research methods of investigation to industrial psychology issues. Topics may include job analysis, job performance appraisal/management, selection/recruitment, and training/development. Legal, ethical, and fairness issues of implementing personnel systems are also considered.

title: Seminar in Organizational Psychology
description: Survey course applying psychological principles and research methods of investigation to organizational behavior issues. Topics include work attitudes/emotions, stress and worker well-being, diversity and fairness, socialization/mentoring, teams, leadership, motivation, power and politics, organizational culture/climate, and organizational development.

title: Seminar in Organizational Research and Ethics
description: Design of field research, quasi-experimental, and non-experimental techniques to address applied psychology questions in organizational settings. Consideration of ethical and professional issues related to organizational research. Selected topic areas within applied psychology include multi-level research, survey research, or program evaluation.

title: Theories and Methods in Developmental Science
description: Philosophical and biological origins of developmental psychology. Examination of processes that shape perception, language acquisition, socialization, and cognition.

title: Advanced Statistics in Psychology
description: Fundamentals of multiple regression and correlation. Principles of experimental design. Analysis of variance including factorial and repeated-measures designs and a priori and post hoc comparisons including trend analysis. Computer-based statistical packages in the analysis of data from psychological research.

title: Advanced Statistics in Psychology
description: Fundamentals of multiple regression and correlation. Principles of experimental design. Analysis of variance including factorial and repeated-measures designs and a priori and post hoc comparisons including trend analysis. Computer-based statistical packages in the analysis of data from psychological research.

title: Seminar in Psychological Measurement
description: General principles, theory and methods underlying measurement in studies of group and individual differences in controlled experiments.

title: Selected Topics in Psychology
description: Intensive study in specific areas of psychology.

title: Advanced Seminar in Industrial Psychology
description: Advanced selected topics course applying psychological principles and research methods of investigation to industrial psychology issues. Topics may include individual differences assessment, selection, and training. Legal, ethical, and fairness issues of implementing and adjusting personnel systems are also considered.
notes: See Class Schedule for specific content

title: Advanced Seminar in Organizational Psychology
description: Advanced selected topics course applying psychological principles and research methods of investigation to organizational behavior issues. Topics may include work attitudes/emotions, stress and worker well-being, diversity/fairness, socialization, teams, leadership, motivation, power/politics, organizational culture/climate, and organizational development.
notes: See Class Schedule for specific content

title: Seminar in Social Psychology
description: Classic and contemporary issues in social psychology including social influence, person perception, attitudes and attitude change, group dynamics, intergroup conflict, and cultural influence.

title: Clinical Psychological Science: Theory and Methods
description: Methodological and theoretical foundations in clinical psychological science. Dissemination/implementation, nosology, and professional issues in clinical psychology.

title: Seminar in Physiological Correlates of Behavior
description: Course may be repeated provided it is offered by a different instructor and the subject matter is substantially different. To enroll in the seminar for the second time, the student must submit a petition to be approved by the professor of the course and the master’s program adviser.

title: Seminar in Cognitive and Behavioral Neuroscience
description: Issues of contemporary importance in neuroscience.

title: Advanced Systems Neuroscience
description: Neuroanatomy and neurophysiology of the mammalian through a signals and systems lens to include auditory, cell physiology, motor and limbic systems, neural development, simple neural models, somatosensory, and visual components. Neuroimaging physics.

title: Advanced Foundations of Neuroimaging
description: Physical and mathematical foundations of diffusion, functional, structural, perfusion MRI, and fMRI time series analysis. Cortical- surface based reconstruction and data analysis. Neural basis, localization, and recording of EEG and MEG signals.

title: Experimental Design and Data Analysis in Behavioral Research
description: Principles and methods of behavioral research stressing interdependence of experimental design and statistical evaluation of results. General linear model in its regression and ANOVA formulations. Advanced multiple regression and correlation techniques using computer-based statistical packages.

title: Experimental Design and Data Analysis in Behavioral Research
description: Principles and methods of behavioral research stressing interdependence of experimental design and statistical evaluation of results. General linear model in its regression and ANOVA formulations. Advanced multiple regression and correlation techniques using computer-based statistical packages.

title: Multivariate Statistics in Psychology
description: Introduction to multivariate techniques. Latent structure models with attention to relationship between latent constructs and observable data. Includes causal models, factor analysis (both exploratory and confirmatory), canonical correlation, path analysis, discriminant function analysis, and loglinear analysis.

title: Multilevel Modeling for Psychological Research
description: Statistical analysis of nested or hierarchical data generated by cross-sectional and longitudinal designs common to psychological science. Examine, critique, and discuss methodological articles regarding multilevel modeling.

title: Seminar in Cognitive Psychology
description: Empirical data, methods, principles, and theories in cognitive psychology.

title: Practicum in the Teaching of Psychology
description: Supervision in the teaching of psychology, covering lecture writing, style of lecture presentation, in-class demonstration and exercise, test and syllabi construction, and grading system. Not applicable to an advanced degree.

title: Internship in Applied Psychology
description: Supervised training in applied psychology in a program approved internship setting.

title: Selected Topics in Psychology
description: Intensive study in specific areas of psychology. In-depth investigation of controversial issues in the field as well as introduction to current and emerging technologies. Cognition, cognitive neuroimaging, and social perception.

title: Research
description: Research in one of the fields of psychology.

title: Special Study
description: Individual projects involving library or laboratory research in any area of psychological investigation or interest.

title: Thesis
description: Preparation of a project or thesis for the master’s degree. Credit is contingent upon acceptance of the completed thesis by the Department of Psychology.

title: Thesis Extension
description: Registration required in any semester or term following assignment of RP in Course 799A in which the student expects to use the facilities and resources of the university; also student must be registered in the course when the completed thesis is granted final approval.

title: Seminar in History and Ethics in Psychology
description: Historical background of modern psychology; in-depth examination of the American Psychological Association code of ethics and its application to the conduct of clinical psychologists.

title: Seminar in Cultural Psychology
description: Cultural origins of human behavior; cultural limits of psychological knowledge.

title: Seminar in Developmental Psychopathology
description: Research and theory in biological and social origins of psychopathology. Methods of assessing developmental change and stability, issues related to vulnerability and resiliency, developmental appropriateness of approaches to interventions, and role of culture as a developmental context.

title: Seminar in Personality and Social Psychology
description: Research and theory in personality and social psychology. Theories of personality and individual differences, group processes, sex roles, social perception, and cross-cultural issues.

title: Behavioral Medicine Seminar: Assessment
description: Assessment methods and issues in behavioral medicine. Development and implementation of assessment plans. Theoretical and practical aspects of psychological, behavioral, and physiological assessment methods for various health issues.

title: Behavioral Medicine Seminar: Intervention
description: Design and implement interventions by stressing empirically supported approaches to improve health and change health behaviors. Strengths and weaknesses of clinical community interventions.

title: Seminar and Laboratory in Counseling and Psychotherapy
description: Supervised practice in application of psychotherapeutic and counseling techniques from selected cognitive, dynamic, interpersonal, and behavioral approaches. Open only to students accepted in the doctoral program.

title: Seminar in Theory and Practice in Clinical Interventions
description: Theory and application of clinical interventions, advanced study of interviewing techniques, behavioral interventions, cognitive/ behavioral interventions, and family/child interventions.

title: Seminar in Experimental Psychopathology Research
description: Analysis of experimental and theoretical literature as it pertains to research methodology for the study of disordered behavior.

title: Seminar in Psychological Assessment I
description: Theory and practice in assessment of intelligence and special abilities. Open only to students accepted in the doctoral program.

title: Seminar in Psychological Assessment II
description: Theory and practice in assessment of special abilities, personality and behavior disorders. Open only to students accepted in the doctoral program.

title: Seminar in Physiological Foundations of Behavior
description: Research and theory in physiological psychology. Advanced study of biological rhythms, sleep and waking, stress responses, the neurophysiology of learning and memory, and research methods in physiological psychology.

title: Advanced Multivariate Statistics
description: Use of multivariate techniques. Relationship between latent constructs and observable data. Analyses such as causal models, exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis, canonical correlation, path analysis, discriminant function analysis, loglinear analysis, and hierarchical linear modeling using computer-based statistical packages.

title: Seminar in Cognition, Affect, and Cognitive-Affective Interactions
description: Research and theory pertaining to interactions among affective and cognitive processes.

title: Clinical Internship
description: Clinical training in an APA-approved internship setting.

title: Practicum in the Teaching of Psychology
description: Supervision in the teaching of psychology, covering lecture writing, style of lecture presentation, in-class demonstration and exercises, test and syllabi construction, and grading systems.

title: Clinical Practicum
description: Supervision of advanced intervention strategies applied to clinical populations.

title: Doctoral Research
description: Independent investigation in the general field of the dissertation.

title: Doctoral Special Study
description: Individual study in the field of specialization.
